definitions.explanation: A woman employed to breast-feed and bring up another woman's child, as was done in noble and wealthy households in the past. Today it is a word of history and stories.

examples.japanese: {乳母|うば}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{育|そだ}てられた→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧。
examples.english: He was raised by a wet nurse.
The princess had a nurse looking after her.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子|こ}ども⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{母親|ははおや}→母親：03564_hahaoya⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：09578_dehanaku⟧{乳母|うば}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{育|そだ}てられる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}かった→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, the children of feudal lords were often brought up by wet nurses rather than by their mothers.

notes:
Also read めのと in classical texts. The reading うば also names an old woman ({姥|うば}), a different word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乳母車|うばぐるま}: baby carriage, pram (old-fashioned; now ⟦ベビーカー→ベビーカー：11154_bebiikaa⟧)
- {乳母日傘|おんばひがさ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{育|そだ}つ→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧: to be brought up pampered, with every comfort

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧: mother
- ⟦{保育士|ほいくし}→保育士：26911_hoikushi⟧: nursery teacher, childcare worker — the modern professional
- ベビーシッター: babysitter
